seoDescription: Learn how to build a beautiful backyard garden pond with a cascading waterfall. This step-by-step guide covers everything from initial planning and site selection to final landscaping. Follow along as we demonstrate how to excavate the site, install a rigid pond shell and a flexible liner for the waterfall, and set up a pump and filter system for clear, circulating water. Discover professional techniques for using decorative rocks, flagstone, and pond foam to create a natural, serene look.

chapters.title: Introduction & Planning Your Pond
chapters.description: Learn the critical factors for choosing the perfect pond location and an overview of the two-tiered pond and waterfall design.

chapters.title: Marking and Excavating the Pond
chapters.description: This chapter covers marking the pond's shape, beginning the excavation, and planning for the displaced dirt.

chapters.title: Digging to Depth and Leveling
chapters.description: Learn how to dig the pond to the correct depth, establish a rough level, and check the pond shell's placement relative to the ground.

chapters.title: Adding a Sand Base
chapters.description: Understand why and how to add a sand base to raise the pond shell and create a smooth, level foundation.

chapters.title: Setting and Securing the Pond Shell
chapters.description: This chapter focuses on placing the pond shell on the leveled sand and backfilling around it to lock it into position.

chapters.title: Building the Waterfall's Foundation
chapters.description: Watch how to build up the base for the waterfall using dirt and sand, ensuring it is level side-to-side and sloped towards the pond.

chapters.title: Installing the Flexible Waterfall Liner
chapters.description: Learn how to position and trim the flexible liner for the waterfall, including the crucial step of draping it into the main pond.

chapters.title: Installing the Pump and Filtration System
chapters.description: Follow the process of placing the pump, positioning and burying the external filter, and connecting the two components with a hose.

chapters.title: Creating the Rock Waterfall
chapters.description: Discover how to use flagstone, smaller rocks, and pond foam to build a natural-looking and watertight waterfall structure.

chapters.title: Hiding the Hose and Final Rock Placement
chapters.description: Learn a clever trick for hiding the waterfall outlet hose with stone and see the different types of rocks used to finish the pond edge.

chapters.title: Cleaning and Detailing the Pond Interior
chapters.description: This chapter covers the final prep work inside the pond, including cleaning the shell, adding a shelf to hide the pump, and rinsing gravel.

chapters.title: Filling the Pond and Final Landscaping
chapters.description: Watch as the pond is filled with water, surrounding landscaping is completed, and the pump is turned on for the first time.

chapters.title: Adding Water Plants and Final Reveal
chapters.description: Learn the benefits of adding water lilies for both aesthetics and pond health, followed by the final reveal of the completed project.

summary:
## Key Concepts for Building a Garden Pond

This document outlines the core steps and considerations for installing a backyard pond with a waterfall, as demonstrated in the video.

### ## Planning Your Pond

- **Location is Crucial**: Choose a spot that is:
  - On **level, well-drained ground**.
  - Near an **electrical outlet** for the pump.
  - Near an **outdoor faucet** for filling.
  - Receives **direct sunlight** for plant variety, but with some shade for fish.
- **Design**: The video features a a **two-tiered design** using a rigid shell for the main pond and a flexible liner for a custom waterfall.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Call **811** before you dig to locate and avoid any underground utility lines like sewer or electrical wires.

### ## Excavation & Preparation

1.  **Mark the Outline**: Place the **rigid shell** and use marking paint to trace its perimeter.
2.  **Dig the Hole**:
    - Excavate **2 inches wider** than the pond shell's shape.
    - Dig **3 inches deeper** than the shell's height (e.g., 21 inches deep for an 18-inch shell).
    - This extra space is for a sand base.
    - Remove all large rocks and roots.
3.  **Create a Sand Base**:
    - Add **3 inches of sand** to the bottom of the excavated hole.
    - Use a rake and a level to create a perfectly **flat and smooth base**.
4. **Set the Pond Shell**:
     - Place the shell on the sand base. The lip should sit **2-3 inches above ground level** to prevent runoff from contaminating the pond.
     - Use a 2x4 and a level to ensure the shell is perfectly level in all directions.
     - **Backfill** around the shell with sand to lock it securely in place.

### ## Installation of Components

- **Waterfall Construction**:
  - Build a mound of dirt to form the base of the waterfall.
  - Add a layer of sand on top, ensuring it's level side-to-side but **slopes toward the pond** front-to-back.
  - Drape a **flexible liner** over the mound, making sure the end hangs down *into* the pond to ensure proper water return.
- **Pump & Filter**:
  - Place the **submersible pump** inside the pond.
  - Bury the **external filter** partially in the ground nearby for easy access and concealment.
  - Connect the pump's outlet to the filter's inlet using **flexible pond hose** and hose clamps.
  - Run a second hose from the filter's outlet up to the top of the waterfall.

### ## Landscaping & Finishing Touches

- **Rock Work**:
  - Use a combination of large **flagstone**, smaller stones, and egg rock to build the waterfall and hide the liners.
  - **Pond foam** acts as an adhesive and sealant, holding rocks in place and directing water flow.
  - A clever trick is to build a small stone "box" to hide the water hose outlet at the top of the waterfall.
- **Pond Interior**:
  - Build a small shelf with flagstone inside the pond to hide the pump.
  - Add **pea gravel** to the ledges and bottom for a more natural look.
- **Water & Plants**:
  - Fill the pond with a standard garden hose.
  - Add **landscaping plants** around the pond to unify the feature with the yard.
  - Place **water lilies** (in their pots) into the pond to provide shade, beauty, and algae control.

> [!TIP]
> Always **rinse gravel and rocks** with a hose before adding them to the pond. This prevents dirt and sediment from making your water cloudy.
